page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Operating under KVM virtualization, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Ampere Altra processor clocked at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 64.0 GB total, delivering 2.0 GB per vCPU in a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data, and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Accelerator hardware is absent, with zero GPUs present.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent parallel scaling across the 32 dedicated ARM cores. The server records an average multi-core CPU score of 57239.02 in stress-ng and 12597.0 in Geekbench. In multi-threaded data decompression via bzip3, throughput reaches 217.66 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested machines. Single-threaded benchmarks, however, represent a clear tradeoff: Geekbench single-core (1072.0), single-threaded gzip compression (23.74 GB/sec), and single-threaded bzip3 (7.55 GB/sec) test within the lower quartile, reflecting the modest per-core clock rate of 2.8 GHz.

Memory subsystem throughput registers at 156.84 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 75.84 GB/sec for large-block writes. Practical application benchmarks demonstrate sustained average throughput, with Redis SET handling 44.07 million operations per second and static web serving achieving 26.4 GB/sec. The system also handles smaller large language model inference, reaching 1063.36 prompt tokens per second on a 135M model and 37.49 prompt tokens per second on a 7B model.

The ecs.c6r.8xlarge offers a cost-effective operational profile for organizations migrating to ARM-native architectures that prioritize core count and steady thread isolation over peak single-core clock frequencies. Workload fit includes scale-out web serving, multi-threaded batch operations, clang software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice architectures.

Configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio suitable for compute-intensive workloads. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network storage attachments, and features an 8 Gbps baseline network interface without GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-threaded execution, evidenced by a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 217.66 GB/sec, alongside average multi-core results across stress-ng and Geekbench suites. Conversely, single-thread metrics fall in lower percentiles due to core clock constraints. The platform functions efficiently for parallel computing workloads, software compilation, Redis key-value workloads, and containerized web infrastructure running on ARM-compatible environments.
